A committee conducts the PST and PFT. It is headed by a Deputy Inspector General of Police and includes officers of Deputy Director rank nominated by the Director General of Police and Director General
with one acting as Member Secretary. Only candidates who qualify in the PST are considered for the PFT. Medical certificates are not taken into account
and the result given by the committee is final. Height and weight are measured with standard machines
and all tests are recorded by videography or CCTV.
Candidates must pass at least 03 of the 05 events. Each event carries 20 marks
and passing an event gives 20 marks. Passing 3
4 or 5 events gives 60
80 or 100 marks respectively. Candidates who refuse to take part in
or fail
all the events are disqualified. After each event
the candidate must check the details entered in the prescribed format and sign it. After the tests
the candidate signs the form and puts a left thumb impression before the committee. Failing this
the candidate is disqualified.

The merit list is prepared from the marks scored in the Physical Fitness Test and the percentage of marks in SSLC or the equivalent examination. A provisional selection list is then prepared in a 1:1 ratio. All candidates in the provisional list must appear before the medical board
at a time and place fixed by the recruitment authority. The medical examination covers:
Vision: near and distant vision under the standards given in the notification (Standard-1
2 or 3
with or without glasses). Each eye must have a full field of vision. Colour blindness
squint or any morbid condition of the eye or eyelid is a disqualification. Hearing: Rinne's Test
Weber's Test and Tests for Vertigo. Any defect found is a disqualification. Physical defects: any one of knock knees
flat foot or bow legs is a physical disqualification. Chest X-ray.
Only candidates certified physically fit by the medical board will be eligible for appointment. Even after passing the PST and PFT
staff of the department must be physically fit and must not have any physical defect or disability that hinders their duties.

how_to_apply: Open the link on the Karnataka Examinations Authority website (https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/) or the department website (https://ksfes.karnataka.gov.in/en).
Read all the instructions on eligibility before filling in the online application.
Fill in the online application between 23.11.2026 and 22.12.2026.
If claiming reservation, enter the correct RD number of the caste or reservation certificate in the online application.
Upload a recent photograph and signature in JPEG format. The photograph must have a white background and a file size of 50 KB to 200 KB. The signature must be 50 KB to 70 KB.
Submit the application. No change or correction is allowed in any detail of a submitted application at any stage.

Applications with wrong or false information will be cancelled at any time without notice, and legal action may be taken. The department and the authority are not responsible for technical problems when applying or paying the fee at the last moment.

Candidates claiming reservation must obtain the certificate from the Tahsildar concerned, valid on the last date for applications. The certificate must bear the Tahsildar's signature and seal, or a barcode, hologram and watermark, and must have an RD number. Originals must be produced at document verification. If a wrong RD number, or another candidate's RD number, is entered and the candidate is disqualified, the authority is not responsible.
Scheduled Caste (with Category-A, B or C certificate and RD number) and Scheduled Tribe candidates: Form 'D'
Category-2A, 2B, 3A and 3B candidates: Form 'F' (valid for 5 years)

Certificates obtained in any other format will be rejected. Under the orders dated 16.07.2011 and 30.03.2002, Balija and its sub-castes must claim 3(A) reservation in the online application for jobs. A 2(A) certificate obtained for education will not be accepted.

Persons serving in the armed forces can apply within one year before completing their term of engagement. They must get a No Objection Certificate from the army before applying, and those already released must hold the release certificate. Originals must be produced at document verification, or the reservation will be cancelled.
Dependants of ex-servicemen who died or were permanently disabled while in service must get the prescribed certificate before applying.

Rural reservation is available only to candidates who studied from Class 1 to Class 10 in areas covered by rural reservation. They must obtain the certificate in Form-1 (with RD number) from the Tahsildar by the last date and enter the RD number in the online application. They must also hold Form-2, signed by the school headmaster and countersigned by the Block Education Officer. General Merit rural candidates must also obtain the Form-1 certificate showing they are not in the creamy layer.
important_instructions: Call letters for the PST and PFT must be downloaded from the department's website. They will not be sent separately, and candidates without a call letter will not be allowed to take the tests. Bring a photocopy of the submitted online application along with the call letter, or you will not be allowed to appear. Bring one photo ID: Passport, Driving Licence, PAN Card, a photo Service ID Card issued by a State or Central Government, PSU or Government-controlled private company, or a photo bank or post office passbook. A registered property document or patta with photo, a caste certificate with photo, an ex-servicemen pension book or PPO, an NREGS job card with photo, EPIC or Aadhaar Card is also accepted. Candidates absent on the fixed date and time are disqualified, and no other date is given. The PST and PFT committee alone decides whether candidates absent through illness get another chance. The selection committee may cancel or add test centres. The time and place are also displayed on the notice boards of the test centres, so check the department website daily. The department and the recruitment committee are not responsible for any accident during the tests. Candidates take part at their own risk and should get a medical check-up and practise for at least one month in advance. At the medical examination, bring originals (SSLC or Class 10 certificate, caste certificate and reservation certificates). Bring also one set of photocopies attested by a Gazetted Officer. No allowance is paid for attending the Physical Fitness Test or the medical examination. Helpline printed in the notice: 080-23460460 (10.00 AM to 6.00 PM).

content_sections.heading: About KSFES Fire Fighter
content_sections.text: Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Services is a department of the Government of Karnataka with its headquarters in Bengaluru. This recruitment is made under the Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Services Department Cadre and Recruitment Rules-2013 and the Karnataka Civil Services (General Recruitment) Rules, 1977, with their amendments and the Government orders listed in the notification. Selected Fire Fighters are trained at the R.A. Mundkur Fire and Emergency Services Academy or the State's fire service training centres.

faq.answer: Candidates are shortlisted 1:5 on SSLC marks and take the PST and PFT. The merit list is based on PFT marks and SSLC percentage, followed by a 1:1 provisional list and a medical examination.

faq.question: Can women apply for KSFES Fire Fighter Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: No. The notification invites online applications from eligible male candidates only.

faq.question: What are the physical standards for KSFES Fire Fighter?
faq.answer: Candidates need a minimum height of 168 cm and a minimum weight of 50 kg. The chest must be at least 81 cm (fully exhaled) with a minimum expansion of 5 cm.
